experiments.scope: The sha256-r40-prefix-v1 target with the 64-byte messages M(x) of proof Section 1 (two blocks after FIPS padding). Each trial runs ONE attempt of the shipped 256-lane search (plan(16): distinguished points with the low 2 bits zero, 7 batches of 256 lanes, cut rule, table, recovery on the rolled two-lane program) on the walk g16(x) = the low 16 bits of the complete digest of M(x), x < 2^16: each batch runs the shipped program on the 256 planes (the 240 high input planes zero) and the experiment's digest network inverts walk B and adds block 2. It returns M(x) and M(y) when the attempt found a pair, two nulls otherwise. Observations (untrusted, the program's own): target_ok, batches, halt.
experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages are distinct and their complete 40-step digests (two blocks) agree in the low 16 bits (digest bytes 30 and 31). This is exact: the attempt merges two trails of a walk whose value is those 16 digest bits. The number of trials that return a pair is reported as a program check; no probability, interval or sampling inference is drawn from it. Not shown: any width-256 cost or success probability.

experiments.scope: The sha256-r40-prefix-v1 target with the 64-byte messages M(x) at full width 256. Each trial evaluates 256 points x with the shipped program (source by trial index mod 3: uniform inputs from the seed, counter inputs r + i, iterates of g from 256 seed-derived starts), forms their complete two-block digests with the experiment's digest network (inverse of walk B, chaining value, block 2), and returns two distinct points whose digests agree in the low 16 bits when the set contains such a pair, two nulls otherwise. Untrusted observations: source, dup_w0 (equal pairs in the low 16 digest bits).
experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages M(x) and M(y) are distinct and their complete 40-step digests agree in the low 16 bits. This is exact: it checks the program, the inverse of walk B, the chaining value, block 2 and the message construction at full width. The counts are program checks, not estimates. Not shown: collision structure at 2^128 evaluations.

experiments.scope: A reduced-width model check of the actual emitted walk g, not the digest-only experiment map. The first 128 organizer trial seeds define 128 observed 20-bit roots. Two lanes per root follow h(x)=g(x) mod 2^20 for at most 2048 evaluations. A point is distinguished when its low 5 bits are zero. A fresh distinguished endpoint is stored as key+1 in the slot indexed by its trail number, and that lane restarts at r+t, matching the submitted table and restart logic at reduced width. The remaining 128 organizer seeds are hashed in order as a committed holdout calibration seed. The program runs 48 complete null ensembles from that holdout. Every ensemble has 128 groups sharing one lazy-sampled uniform 20-bit function and uses the same two-lane, distinguished-point, table, and restart procedure. It returns null message pairs because this is distributional evidence, not a collision event.
experiments.hypothesis: The collision statistic is Pearson sum((observed-expected)^2/expected) over four 512-evaluation bins and one censored bin, where expected is the mean of the 48 complete shared-function ensembles. Each null ensemble is scored against the leave-one-out mean of the other 47. px is its add-one empirical upper-tail rank. The DP statistic counts outputs only for inputs globally fresh across all 128 groups, standardizes against density 1/32, and calibrates absolute z by the same add-one complete-ensemble rank pz. The source hard-asserts px>=0.05 and pz>=0.05. The first organizer-visible observation exports the holdout commitment, ensemble count, observed bins, both statistics, and both calibrated ranks. Passing supports H1's random-mapping first-collision and DP-density clauses at width 20 under the scaled adaptive table logic. It does not prove either clause at width 256 or test 2^128-scale behavior.
